title: Can a PNG Be HDR? Choose the Photo Export Goal
description: PNG can hold SDR or HDR image information. Choose your photo export goal on iPhone separately from transparency, compression and the file extension.
direct: PNG can contain SDR or HDR image information. Choose the dynamic range you want to deliver separately from the settings for transparency and file type.

cards.decision.heading: A bright PNG can be valid
cards.decision.body: An unexpectedly bright PNG is not necessarily a display fault. The current PNG specification includes color signaling and HDR-related metadata. The image, viewing app and display must work together to determine its appearance.
sections.detail-0-0.heading: Three properties can vary independently
sections.detail-0-0.body: PNG’s lossless compression describes how its encoded image data is stored. Transparency describes whether pixels can reveal a background. Dynamic range describes a different aspect of the represented light.
sections.detail-0-1.heading: Keep transparency separate from brightness
sections.detail-0-1.body: Preserving transparency does not make an HDR source into SDR, and lossless compression does not mean a color conversion is reversible.
sections.detail-1-0.heading: Choose the intended result
sections.detail-1-0.body: Its public version offers normal and HDR workflows, including PNG export. The first three successful photo conversions are free; each batch photo counts separately.
sections.detail-1-1.heading: Check how HDR displays
sections.detail-1-1.body: The app’s normal-to-HDR mode is a creative brightness effect and cannot recover lost scene detail. This guide does not claim which exact PNG metadata chunks the app writes or promise identical brightness across viewers. The illustration explains format versus export intent, rather than demonstrating actual HDR light output.
faqs.reader-question-1.heading: If a PNG keeps transparency, is it also HDR?
faqs.reader-question-1.body: Transparency controls which parts show a background. HDR describes light representation. Either property can be checked independently.
faqs.reader-question-2.heading: Why does the same PNG look less bright in another viewer?
faqs.reader-question-2.body: The viewer or display may render its brightness differently. Test the intended destination, and make a separate SDR copy if that is what it needs.

related.related.label: How to convert HDR photos to normal SDR on iPhone
steps.step-1.text: Decide whether you need a standard SDR sharing copy or an intentional HDR image. Check the destination’s requirements instead of selecting PNG solely because you associate it with screenshots.
steps.step-2.text: In PhotoFix: HDR to Normal Photos, choose HDR to normal photo for SDR delivery, then select PNG when you need that format or transparency. Keep the original.
steps.step-3.text: Inspect the saved file in the intended app and on the target display when possible. If you choose a creative HDR export instead, verify its appearance on a compatible HDR display.
